newsitem.title: USA: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-SUPER BOWL ACCIDENT WON'T CHANGE HALFTIME SHOWS.
newsitem.headline: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-SUPER BOWL ACCIDENT WON'T CHANGE HALFTIME SHOWS.

text.p: The commissioner of the National Football League denied on Friday that the extravegant halftime shows at the Super Bowl had become dangerous -- despite the death of a performer in a rehearsal for Sunday's game.

Commissioner Paul Tagliabue refused to acknowledge that the glittering shows -- which in the past have featured fireworks displays, sky-divers and helicopters landing on, and taking off from the playing field -- had gotten out of control.
Tagliabue spoke to reporters a day after a 43-year-old woman, part of a professional bungee-jumping team, suffered a fatal head injury while practicing their act in the Louisiana Superdome stadium.
The elasticised bungee cord apparently stretched more than expected, and the woman struck her head several times on the stadium floor.
"Any time you have a tragic accident, you have to think a lot," Tagliabue said when asked if the NFL would reconsider its approach to halftime shows.
The shows are designed to keep hundreds of millions of television viewers glued to their screens during the intermission -- when advertisements are shown that bring the league millions of dollars.

While Tagliabue called the accident "a tragedy" and express condolences to the woman's family -- her husband and sister are part of the jumping team -- he would not admit that maybe the league had gone "too far" in trying to come up with new ideas every year.
Tagliabue did say, however, that the bungee-jumping part of Sunday's halftime show -- which would have been the finale -- had been scrapped.
"That portion of the finale will be omitted -- for obvious reasons," he said.

"They are entertainers. No one is forcing them to perform," he said, apparently speaking generally of the participants in the shows, which usually take place at night in stadiums filled with tens of thousands of spectators.
"It (the accident) probably will not change our approach to Super Bowl halftimes," Tagliabue said. "But we will make sure our approach is safe."
He added that there would be some sort of "appropriate" memorial for the woman, Laura Patterson of Sarasota, Fla., but the details had not been decided.
Tagliabue said that police had not yet determined how the woman fell to her death while rehearsing on Thursday night.
"The New Orleans Police Department is still investigating. I'd rather not speculate," he said.
